It is the only ERP line on the trip, and the trip record's own routing-engine output puts the optimal route's ERP at SGD 0.00 (optimal_route_source: routing-engine-v3.2).

POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The closest any fix on the driver's trace comes to this gantry is 11,401.84 m — fix index 0, at 15:09:20, the very first fix of the trip — and the derived proximity block records that the closest approach is not bracketed by any trace gap. Not one of the 108 fixes falls anywhere near the match radius, so the vehicle never crossed this gantry.

That negative finding is a real absence, not a hole in the data. Under POL-RD-07 the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 108 fixes, a 10.0 s sample interval against a 10.0 s expected interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. There is no stretch of the disputed segment in which a gantry crossing could have gone unrecorded.

The fare artifact itself flags this gantry on_optimal_route = false, and POL-RD-02 builds the chargeable ERP into the fare only for gantries 'lying on the optimal route'. On either measure — the trace the driver's own vehicle produced, or the platform's own optimal route — the SGD 2.00 line is a charge for a gantry this trip does not use.

The rider does not need a deviation to recover this line. POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) 'whether or not a deviation exists', and on this record none exists: the governing trace figure is 13.65 km against a 13.0 km optimal, an excess of 0.65 km (5.00%), short of both the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% gate. The rider's case therefore stands on the unmatched charge line alone, and is not overstated as a route-deviation claim.

POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The line is SGD 2.00, so the standalone correction is SGD 2.00; the balance of the contested SGD 3.50 is distance and time, and no clause on this record returns any of it because POL-RD-02 never runs without an established deviation.

Because the refund issues under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-10(8) does not fire: its escalation trigger for a charge line with no counterpart in the trace expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). Under POL-GEN-03 this is a referral attached to a monetary ruling, not an escalation — the SGD 2.00 moves and the case does not go to a human reviewer to be held.

The driver's only answer is 'The ERP is charged by the system', which cites no evidence ID and no clause; under POL-RD-08 an assertion from either side that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. No traffic explanation can fill the gap either: the bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-03106-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, so no advisory covers this corridor and POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable on the record. The chat log for the trip is empty (0 messages), so no rider instruction sent the vehicle anywhere near this gantry. Disclosure: the only impaired artifact I cite is EV-ADVIS-03106-01, at weight 0.0, and I cite it for its absence, not for any fact it carries.

The rider is not a serial claimant, and the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay is not engaged: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the additional corroboration POL-RD-08 requires where the 60-day claim counter is 4 or more does not apply. The rider's claim rests on the artifacts themselves, and they support it.

claims.text: The deviation the rider's complaint implies does not exist on this trip's own trace. The gps_trace measures 13.65 km against a booking-time optimal route of 13.0 km, an excess of 0.65 km, or 5.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to be passed before a route deviation is ESTABLISHED: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal_distance_km (here 2.6 km) and must exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms. It fails both, and it fails them on the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing over the rounded trip_record copy. On either figure the answer is the same, so the rider's characterisation of the trip cannot open a deviation case.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and cannot discharge it. Limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or from an independent source where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). Neither route is open: the trace here is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — 108 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a 10 s sampling interval matching the 10 s expected interval, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0.0 s — so there is no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling above 30 s, and the impaired-trace escape in POL-RD-07 is simply not available. The measured excess is 5.0%, so limb (b) fails on the merits as well as on the measurement.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider on those lines. The fare_breakdown carries a derived recomputed_fare of 19.2780 and a derived refund of 2.5820, but POL-RD-02 is expressly conditioned on a deviation being established under POL-RD-01; without establishment that arithmetic is a counterfactual and is not a licensed remedy. charged_total was 21.86, and the metered distance and time lines stand: the rider was billed 13.7 km against a 13.65 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall to correct either.

The only line the rider's complaint actually identifies is the SGD 2.00 AYE Alexandra Rd gantry pass-through, and ERP is settled exclusively under POL-RD-09 as a standalone, government-set pass-through itemised separately from distance and time. Three limits follow and they cap the driver's exposure on this case: (i) the correction can attach only to that SGD 2.00 line and cannot be blended into, or multiplied through, a distance refund; (ii) it is settled under POL-RD-09 and receives no POL-RD-02 or POL-RD-06 uplift, because ERP is a pass-through at metered cost that is never surged or uplifted; and (iii) it is no part of the SGD 3.50 the rider contests, so nothing in this record supports a refund beyond that single line.

No POL-RD-06 consequence can attach to this driver on this trip. POL-RD-06 is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and 0.65 km / 5.0% is far below the POL-RD-01 materiality gate of 8.0 km or 50% of optimal, so the clause is not triggered at all. Even if the tribunal ran the check, the only fields POL-RD-06 permits it to use show no pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 305, so there is neither the three-flag trigger nor a 0.05 ratio. Neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) is available, and no other profile field may be used to establish anything about this trip.

The driver asserts no external traffic cause and none is needed, so no escalation is available to the rider on this record. The bundle's only traffic_advisory, EV-ADVIS-03106-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 on issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and can carry no fact; but because the excess is below the POL-RD-01 threshold there is nothing for POL-RD-03 to exonerate, and the absent advisory is therefore immaterial. The driver's counterparty statement attributes the ERP line to the system rather than to any closure or queue, and under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that names no advisory evidence ID cannot be invoked against a cited artifact, so the missing-advisory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04. To the rider and to the driver: the two of you agree on most of the law here, and the case turns on one line of the fare.

WHAT I FOUND. Trip TRP-03106 ran 2026-08-28, 15:09:20 to 15:27:10, from Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru to Blk 25 Ghim Moh Link. The fare charged was SGD 21.86 (EV-FARE-03106, total_charged), and SGD 3.50 of it was contested.

THE ROUTE-DEVIATION PART FAILS. The governing trace distance is 13.65 km (EV-GPS-03106) against the booking-time optimal of 13.0 km (EV-TRIP-03106): an excess of 0.65 km, or 5.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal before a deviation is established, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-02 never runs — there is no distance-or-time refund. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 either: 108 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a 10 s sampling interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. Its silence about the gantry is therefore a real absence, not a hole in the data.

THE ERP LINE SUCCEEDS. The fare carries one ERP charge, SGD 2.00 for the 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at 15:18:20, and the gantry's own coordinates sit on the fare line (lat 1.224147, lng 103.893859). POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of it as a crossing. The closest any of the 108 fixes comes to this gantry is 11,401.84 m — over 11 km (EV-GPS-03106, derived.erp_gantry_proximity). The charge is therefore for a gantry this trip never crossed. POL-RD-09(4) makes that a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a referral below. That is SGD 2.00 back to the rider. The remaining SGD 1.50 of the contested amount is distance and time, and no clause on this record returns any of it.

THE DRIVER'S ANSWER. The driver's statement that 'the ERP is charged by the system' cites no evidence ID and no clause, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03106-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I name it because POL-GEN-02 requires impaired artifacts to be disclosed — but because the driver names no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) governs: an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and the POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is not engaged. POL-RD-10(8) does not fire either, because its exception covers exactly this situation, a charge line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 applies.

PROFILES. The driver profile was checked: no material deviation is recorded (0.65 km and 5.0% are far below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality gate), and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 305, so no POL-RD-06 pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise. On the rider side, deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay is not engaged. No other profile field was used, per POL-GEN-01.

OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.00 to the rider, read off the SGD 2.00 ERP component of the SGD 21.86 charged_total, against SGD 3.50 contested. No driver compensation: the fare billed 13.7 km against a 13.65 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. The trace carries the deciding facts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-03106 and EV-FARE-03106), so my confidence is not capped below 0.90. The SGD 2.00 is within the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05) and executes on issue.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the arithmetic of this trip is not really in dispute, and the case turns on a single charge line.

What the trace and the fare agree on. The trip was metered (fare_model METERED) with charged_total SGD 21.86. The governing trace figure on EV-GPS-03106 is 13.65 km against the booking-time optimal of 13.0 km on EV-TRIP-03106 — an excess of 0.65 km, or 5.00%. POL-RD-01 requires both gates to pass (more than 0.8 km AND more than 20%); 0.65 km and 5.00% fail both. No route deviation is established, so the rider's characterisation of the trip as a detour is accepted only in the narrow sense the rider themselves framed it (rider claim 5), and POL-RD-02 never runs: no distance or time refund is available on the SGD 3.50 contested (driver claims 1, 2 and 3 accepted). The driver's side is right that the billed distance (13.7 km) against the 13.65 km trace leaves no unbilled-distance shortfall, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION arises either.

The line that does not survive. The rider's complaint identifies the SGD 2.00 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' entry charged at 15:18:20 on EV-FARE-03106. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing. The closest of the 108 fixes is 11,401.84 m away (fix index 0 at 15:09:20), and the fare artifact itself records on_optimal_route = false. The rider's claim that the vehicle never crossed this gantry (rider claim 2) is accepted. The negative finding is a real absence, not a hole in the data: EV-GPS-03106 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — 100.0% coverage, 10.0 s sample interval against 10.0 s expected, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (rider claim 3 accepted). Under POL-RD-09(4) an unmatched gantry line is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists (POL-RD-01). That is the SGD 2.00.

The balance of the SGD 3.50 contested is distance and time, and no clause on this record returns any of it, because POL-RD-02 is conditioned on an established deviation (rider claim 6 and driver claim 4 accepted; the driver's point that the correction cannot be blended into a distance refund is correct).

The driver's answer. The counterparty statement, 'The ERP is charged by the system', names no evidence ID and no clause and does not defend the line; under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence carries no weight (rider claim 8 accepted). The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03106-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0; it carries no fact and is cited only for its absence. Because the driver asserts no external traffic cause and names no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) applies: no advisory is invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire, and POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable (driver claim 6 and rider claim 7 accepted). POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered, because its only unmatched line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4). No POL-RD-06 consequence attaches: the deviation is nowhere near MATERIAL (0.65 km / 5.00% against 8.0 km / 50%), and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 305, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the conduct referral is available (driver claim 5 accepted). The rider's profile overlay under POL-RD-08 is not engaged either — deviation_claims_60d is 0 — and neither profile changes the outcome (rider claim 9 accepted).

Referral. POL-RD-09(4) requires the unmatched-gantry finding to be recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the referrals list; it rides with the money and is not an escalation under POL-GEN-03.

Figures used: charged_total 21.86; the refunded line 2.00; the contested 3.50; trace distance 13.65 km against optimal 13.0 km (excess 0.65 km / 5.00%); nearest fix to the gantry 11,401.84 m against the 250 m match radius. Confidence is 0.95: the deciding fact is carried by EV-GPS-03106 and EV-FARE-03106, both at weight 1.0, and the MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact and so does not cap it. The monetary effect of SGD 2.00 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically under POL-GEN-05; either party may appeal within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The closest any fix on the driver's trace comes to this gantry is 11,401.84 m — fix index 0, at 15:09:20, the very first fix of the trip — and the derived proximity block records that the closest approach is not bracketed by any trace gap. Not one of the 108 fixes falls anywhere near the match radius, so the vehicle never crossed this gantry.

That negative finding is a real absence, not a hole in the data. Under POL-RD-07 the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 108 fixes, a 10.0 s sample interval against a 10.0 s expected interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. There is no stretch of the disputed segment in which a gantry crossing could have gone unrecorded.

The fare artifact itself flags this gantry on_optimal_route = false, and POL-RD-02 builds the chargeable ERP into the fare only for gantries 'lying on the optimal route'. On either measure — the trace the driver's own vehicle produced, or the platform's own optimal route — the SGD 2.00 line is a charge for a gantry this trip does not use.

The rider does not need a deviation to recover this line. POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) 'whether or not a deviation exists', and on this record none exists: the governing trace figure is 13.65 km against a 13.0 km optimal, an excess of 0.65 km (5.00%), short of both the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% gate. The rider's case therefore stands on the unmatched charge line alone, and is not overstated as a route-deviation claim.

POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The line is SGD 2.00, so the standalone correction is SGD 2.00; the balance of the contested SGD 3.50 is distance and time, and no clause on this record returns any of it because POL-RD-02 never runs without an established deviation.

Because the refund issues under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-10(8) does not fire: its escalation trigger for a charge line with no counterpart in the trace expressly excepts a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). Under POL-GEN-03 this is a referral attached to a monetary ruling, not an escalation — the SGD 2.00 moves and the case does not go to a human reviewer to be held.

The driver's only answer is 'The ERP is charged by the system', which cites no evidence ID and no clause; under POL-RD-08 an assertion from either side that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. No traffic explanation can fill the gap either: the bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-03106-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, so no advisory covers this corridor and POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable on the record. The gps_trace measures 13.65 km against a booking-time optimal route of 13.0 km, an excess of 0.65 km, or 5.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to be passed before a route deviation is ESTABLISHED: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal_distance_km (here 2.6 km) and must exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms. It fails both, and it fails them on the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing over the rounded trip_record copy. On either figure the answer is the same, so the rider's characterisation of the trip cannot open a deviation case.

No POL-RD-06 consequence can attach to this driver on this trip. POL-RD-06 is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and 0.65 km / 5.0% is far below the POL-RD-01 materiality gate of 8.0 km or 50% of optimal, so the clause is not triggered at all. Even if the tribunal ran the check, the only fields POL-RD-06 permits it to use show no pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 305, so there is neither the three-flag trigger nor a 0.05 ratio.
